well: Agassiz77 borehole, Agassiz Ice Cap, Ellesmere Island, Canadian Arctic North (approx 80.7 N, -73.1 E per database metadata); drilled/measured 1977
operator_on_log: Canadian ice-core program lineage (Fisher/Clarke/Waddington; Zdanowicz-provided data per database metadata)
source_database: Greenland and Canadian Arctic ice temperature profiles database (GEUS): Lokkegaard et al. 2023, The Cryosphere 17, 3829-3845, doi:10.5194/tc-17-3829-2023; data DOI 10.22008/FK2/3BVF9V (GEUS Dataverse); science lineage: Clarke, Fisher & Waddington 1987 (IAHS vol. 170, 169-180); redistributed in the public GEUS GitHub repository (boreholes/Agassiz77/data.csv)

coverage: COMPLETE FILE: all 67 stations, 10.91-340.91 m at 5 m spacing, verbatim (database-stated coverage 97% of the 341 m thickness). Database metadata notes: ice thickness in data does not match Vinther (2008) and the location is approximate - carried honestly as the database's own caveat.
curves: t (temperature, degC) - MEASURED TEMPERATURE, 5 m stations
temperature_data: Second continuous MEASURED temperature profile: 67 stations, -24.16 degC near surface warming monotonically below ~16 m to -16.74 degC at 340.91 m - a classic High Arctic ice-cap thermal profile (no deep glacial minimum: the cap is thin relative to GISP2).
dialect_notes: GEUS d,t CSV with space-after-comma values (parser handles); the catalogue's second temperature-CSV entry.
purpose: seventh catalogue entry - SEVENTH region (CANADA, Ellesmere Island); second MEASURED_CURVES-tier well; 1977 vintage (the catalogue's oldest measurement)
verified: 67 stations; endpoints verbatim; MEASURED_CURVES derivation; gate-pinned
